1:2.headline: A kiss on the mouth, not on the hand
1:2.body: Ibn Ezra makes a grammar point. When the verb for kissing takes its object directly, as here, the kiss is on the mouth. With the letter ל ('to') it is on the hand, shoulder or cheek. Rashi says the same: she longs to be kissed mouth to mouth, as at first.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 1:2:1
sources.quote: בלי אות מבדיל בין הדבקים היא בפה כמו ישקני ובאות למ״ד ביד או בכתף או בלחי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a kiss with no linking letter, as in ישקני, is on the mouth, and with ל it is on the hand, shoulder or cheek.

sources.quote: אַךְ אֲנִי מִתְאַוָּה וְשׁוֹקֶקֶת לִהְיוֹתוֹ נוֹהֵג עִמִּי כַמִּנְהָג הָרִאשׁוֹן, כְּחָתָן אֶל כַּלָּה, פֶּה אֶל פֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says she longs for him to treat her as at first, like a groom with a bride, mouth to mouth.

1:2.headline: Maimonides reads the kiss as knowing God with intense love
1:2.body: The Guide for the Perplexed says the sages took 'kisses' here as a poetic name for grasping God with great love. That is why they say Moses, Aaron and Miriam died 'by a kiss'.

sources.quote: הלכו במימרה זו על הדרך השירית המפורסמת המכנה את ההשגה הבאה עם עוצמת החשק בו יתעלה "נשיקה
sources.says: Maimonides says the sages followed the well-known poetic way of calling the grasp of God that comes with intense love a 'kiss'.

sources.quote: ששלשתם מתו בנשיקה
sources.says: He notes the sages' saying that Moses, Aaron and Miriam all died by a kiss.

1:2.headline: Your love, or the sweetness of your mouth?
1:2.body: Metzudat Zion reads דודים as love and affection. Ibn Ezra reports that one of the Geonim read it as the moisture under the tongue, from the phrase 'let us drink our fill of דודים'.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 1:2:1
sources.quote: דודיך. ענין אהבה וחיבה כמו נרוה דודים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means love and affection.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 1:2:2
sources.quote: ואמ׳ אחד מהגאוני׳ שהוא הריר שתחת הלשון מטעם לכה נרוה דודים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that one of the Geonim said it is the moisture under the tongue, because of 'come, let us drink our fill of דודים'.

1:3.headline: Your name is poured-out oil: שם and שמן
1:3.body: The verse sets שמן, oil, next to שם, name. Rashi says a good name is called after good oil. Perfume in a sealed flask gives no smell until it is poured out, and then it spreads far.

sources.quote: שֵׁם טוֹב נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם 'שֶׁמֶן טוֹב
sources.says: Rashi says a good name is named after good oil.

sources.quote: בְּכָל עֵת שֶׁהוּא בִצְלוֹחִית חֲתוּמָה, אֵין רֵיחוֹ נוֹדֵף, פּוֹתְחָהּ וּמֵרִיק שַׁמְנָהּ לִכְלִי אַחֵר, רֵיחוֹ נוֹדֵף
sources.says: Rashi says fine oil gives no scent in a sealed flask, but once poured into another vessel its scent spreads.

1:4.headline: Loved 'with an upright love', or 'more than smooth wine'?
1:4.body: Rashi reads מישרים as a straight, honest love with no crooked turns. Ibn Ezra says it describes the wine, as in wine that 'goes down smoothly'. Then the line means they love you more than smooth wine.

sources.quote: אַהֲבָה עַזָּה, אַהֲבַת מִישׁוֹר בְּלִי עֲקִיבָה וּרְכָסִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is a strong, level love, with no crookedness or rough ground.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 1:4:2
sources.quote: מישרים. הנכון שהוא תאר היין כמו הולך לדודי למישרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the right reading is that the word describes the wine, as in 'goes down smoothly'.

1:6.headline: Very dark, or only a little dark?
1:6.body: The word repeats letters of שחור, black. Metzudat Zion says the repeat adds: she is very dark. Ibn Ezra says it takes away, like אדמדם, 'reddish': she is only darkish.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 1:6:2
sources.quote: בהכפל העי״ן והלמ״ד ויורה על רוב השחרות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the doubled letters show a great deal of blackness.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 1:6:1
sources.quote: שחרחרת. בא הכפל לגרוע ולא להוסיף כמו אדמדמת שהוא מעט אדום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the doubling lessens rather than adds, like אדמדמת, which is a little red.

1:7.headline: Wrapped like a mourner, or darting about?
1:7.body: Rashi reads עטיה as a mourner, wrapped up to the lip and crying. Metzudat Zion reads it as swooping and flying about. Ibn Ezra lists three readings, darting, ashamed or wrapped, and prefers wrapped.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֶהְיֶה כַאֲבֵלָה עוֹטָה עַל שָׂפָה, בּוֹכִיָּה עַל צֹאנִי
sources.says: Rashi says she would be like a mourner wrapped to the lip, crying over her flock.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 1:7:5
sources.quote: כעטיה. ענין הפרחה ושטיפה כמו ותעט אל השלל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means flying and sweeping along, as in 'you swooped on the spoil'.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 1:7:3
sources.quote: והנכון בעיני שהוא מן ועוטך עטה כבגד יעטה
sources.says: After listing other views, Ibn Ezra says the right one is 'wrapped', as one wraps on a garment.

1:9.headline: 'I compared you', or, in a midrash, 'I silenced you'
1:9.body: Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion read דמיתיך as 'I likened you'. Rashi brings a midrash that reads it from דמם, 'be still': at the sea God quieted Israel's cries, as it says 'and you shall hold your peace'.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 1:9:2
sources.quote: דמיתיך. המשלתיך כמו ואל מי תדמיון אל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means 'I compared you', as in 'to whom will you liken God'.

sources.quote: שָׁם 'דִּמִּיתִיךְ רַעְיָתִי', שִׁתַּקְתִּיךְ מִצַּעֲקָתֵךְ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִשׁוּן". זֹאת רָאִיתִי בְּסִפְרֵי אַגָּדָה
sources.says: Rashi says that, in books of midrash, he saw it read as 'I silenced you from your crying', as in 'and you shall hold your peace'.

1:10.headline: Rows of jewels, or shaped figures? A word with no match
1:10.body: Rashi says תורים are rows of earrings and a gold band. Others read the word from תאר, 'shape'. Ibn Ezra says it has no match anywhere except the next verse, 'rows of gold'.

sources.quote: שׁוּרוֹת נִזְמֵי אֹזֶן וּמִצְחַת זָהָב
sources.says: Rashi says these are rows of earrings and a gold forehead band.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 1:10:1
sources.quote: והקרו׳ אלי שאין לו חבר כי אם בספר אחד והוא אחריו תורי זהב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the likeliest view is that the word has no partner except right after it, in 'rows of gold'.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 1:10:3
sources.quote: בתורים. הם הפנינים המסודרים בתואר נאה ותכונה יפה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are pearls set in a fine shape and order.

1:12.headline: Reclining at his table, or in his round palace?
1:12.body: Metzudat Zion reads מסב as the couch where one leaned to eat: the king is at his meal. Ibn Ezra reads it as a round, costly building, as in 'the surroundings of Jerusalem'.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 1:12:2
sources.quote: במסבו. דרכו היה להסב ולהשען על המטות בשעת האכילה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the king's way was to recline on couches while eating.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 1:12:1
sources.quote: במסבו. כמו [ו]מסבי ירושלם הבנין העגול היקר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like 'the surroundings of Jerusalem': the precious round building.

1:12.headline: 'Gave off its scent' is a gentle way to say 'spoiled'
1:12.body: Rashi reads this as Israel's sin with the golden calf, while God's presence was still at Sinai. The nard really 'stank'. Scripture says 'gave its scent' out of love and clean speech.

sources.quote: חִלּוּף לְהַבְאִישׁ, בְּעוֹד שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה בְסִינַי, קִלְקַלְתִּי בָעֵגֶל". וּלְשׁוֹן חִבָּה כָּתַב הַכָּתוּב, "נָתַן רֵיחוֹ", וְלֹא כָתַב "הִבְאִישׁ" אוֹ "הִסְרִיחַ
sources.says: Rashi says 'gave its scent' stands for 'stank': Israel sinned with the calf while God was at Sinai, and the verse used a loving phrase instead of 'stank'.

1:16.headline: Our bed: a real bed, or the Tabernacle?
1:16.body: Maimonides uses this verse to prove that ערש means a bed, when he discusses the size of Og's bed. Rashi reads 'our bed' as the Tabernacle and the Temple, which Scripture also calls a bed.

sources.quote: כי "עֶרֶשׂ" היא המיטה: "אַף עַרְשֵׂנוּ רַעֲנָנָה
sources.says: Maimonides says ערש is a bed, citing 'our bed is fresh'.

sources.quote: הַמִּשְׁכָּן קָרוּי מִטָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "הִנֵּה מִטָּתוֹ שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹה
sources.says: Rashi says the Tabernacle is called a bed, as in 'behold the bed of Solomon'.

2:1.headline: שושנת is named for שש, six, its six petals
2:1.body: Metzudat Zion says the flower is called this because it always has six petals. Ibn Ezra says it may be named that for having six leaves.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 2:1:3
sources.quote: שושנת. שם צמח המריח ונקראת כן על כי היא לעולם בעלת ששה עלין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שושנת is a fragrant plant, and is called so because it always has six petals.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 2:1:2
sources.quote: שנקראת כן בעבור שהיא בעלת שש עלים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may be called so because it has six leaves.

2:4.headline: בית היין: the Tent of Meeting, or a place of public love?
2:4.body: Rashi says the house of wine is the Tent of Meeting, where the details and explanations of the Torah were given. Metzudat David says it is a place where the beloved shows his affection in public. Malbim says the wine here is the wine of prophecy.

sources.quote: אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁשָּׁם נִתְּנוּ פְרָטֶיהָ וּבֵאוּרֶיהָ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is the Tent of Meeting, where the details and explanations of the Torah were given.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 2:4:1
sources.quote: להתענג בי במקום רואים לפרסם חיבתך אלי
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is to delight in me in a place where people see, to make your love for me known.

sources.quote: היין המוזכר בכל הספר הזה ששתתה הרעיה ע"י דודה היא היין הנבואיי המשומר בענביו
sources.says: Malbim says the wine mentioned throughout this book is the prophetic wine, kept in its grapes.

2:4.headline: הביאני: "he brought me", or "bring me"?
2:4.body: Metzudat Zion says it is a past form standing for the future, so it means "bring me". Metzudat David also reads it as a wish. Malbim reads it as a plain story: he took me and brought me to the house of wine.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 2:4:1
sources.quote: הביאני. עבר במקום עתיד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הביאני is the past in place of the future.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 2:4:1
sources.quote: מתאווה אני שתביא אותי אל בית היין
sources.says: Metzudat David says I long that you bring me to the house of wine.

sources.quote: לקחה דודה והביאני אל בית היין
sources.says: Malbim says her beloved took her and brought her to the house of wine.

2:5.headline: רפדוני: spread bedding for me, or support me?
2:5.body: Rashi says רפידה means a bed or mattress, so spread my bedding with apples. Metzudat Zion agrees, citing רפדתי יצועי. Ibn Ezra adds that in the language of Kedar it means "support me".

sources.quote: רְפִידָה לְשׁוֹן מַצָּע הִיא
sources.says: Rashi says רפידה is the language of a bed-covering.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 2:5:2
sources.quote: רפדוני. ענין הצעת המטה כמו רפדתי יצועי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says רפדוני means making up the bed, as in רפדתי יצועי.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 2:5:3
sources.quote: ובלשון קדר (כמו) סעדוני [או חזקוני]
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says in the language of Kedar it is like סעדוני, or strengthen me.

2:7.headline: עד here: "until", or "while"?
2:7.body: Metzudat David reads it as "until": do not stir the love until it comes back by itself. Rashi reads עד as "while", like עד שהמלך במסבו: as long as it is lodged in my heart and he wants me.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 2:7:1
sources.quote: עד שתהיה האהבה נחפצת לשוב אלי מעצמה
sources.says: Metzudat David says until the love is wanted and returns to me by itself.

sources.quote: בְּכָל עוֹד שֶׁהִיא תְקוּעָה בְלִבִּי וְהוּא חָפֵץ בִּי
sources.says: Rashi says it means as long as it is lodged in my heart and he wants me.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ "עַד שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ בִּמְסִבּוֹ", בְּעוֹד שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ בִּמְסִבּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is like עד שהמלך במסבו, meaning while the king is at his table.

2:8.headline: מדלג and מקפץ: one speed said twice, or two kinds of leap?
2:8.body: Metzudat Zion says both words mean dancing and quick going, and the doubling shows how fast he is. Malbim says they differ: first he leaps from mountain to mountain, then jumps from a mountain to the hill below.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 2:8:2
sources.quote: מדלג. מקפץ שניהם ענין רקוד ומהירות ההליכה והכפל במלות שונות יורה על מרבית המהירות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says both words mean dancing and quick going, and the doubling in different words shows the greatest speed.

sources.quote: והוא מדלג על ההרים מהר להר, ומשם מקפץ מן ההר אל הגבעה שתחתיו
sources.says: Malbim says he leaps over the mountains from mountain to mountain, and from there jumps from the mountain to the hill below it.

2:12.headline: הנצנים: flower buds, or Moses and Aaron?
2:12.body: Rashi, reading plainly, says the trees put out flowers. In his explanation of the allegory he says it means Moses and Aaron, ready for you. Ibn Ezra also says Moses and Aaron. Metzudat Zion says the word means a flower, as in עלתה נצה.

sources.quote: קָרְבוּ יְמֵי הַחַמָּה, שֶׁהָאִילָנוֹת מוֹצִיאִין פְּרָחִים
sources.says: Rashi says the days of the sun drew near, when the trees put out flowers.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 2:12:1
sources.quote: הנצנים. ענין פרח כמו עלתה נצה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הנצנים means a flower, as in עלתה נצה.

sources.quote: הֲרֵי משֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן מוּכָנִים לָכֶם לְכָל צָרְכֵיכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says, see, Moses and Aaron are ready for you, for all your needs.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 2:12:3
sources.quote: הנצנים. משה ואהרן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הנצנים are Moses and Aaron.

2:13.headline: The extra yod in לכי stands for ten
2:13.body: The written form has an extra yod: לכי, where we read לך. Rashi says it points to "rise to receive the Ten Commandments".

sources.quote: קוּמִי לָכְי. כְּתִיב יו"ד יְתֵרָה, "קוּמִי לָךְ" לְקַבֵּל עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it is written with an extra yod, and means "rise" to receive the Ten Commandments.

2:14.headline: Why a dove: hunted, or faithful to one mate?
2:14.body: Rashi says Israel was like a dove fleeing a hawk into a crack in the rock, with a snake hissing inside. Metzudat David and Ralbag say the dove is loyal: it does not exchange its mate.

sources.quote: לְיוֹנָה שֶׁבּוֹרַחַת מִפְּנֵי הַנֵּץ וְנִכְנְסָה בִנְקִיקֵי הַסְּלָעִים, וְהָיָה הַנָּחָשׁ נוֹשֵׁף בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says they were like a dove fleeing from a hawk into the cracks of the rocks, with the snake hissing at her.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 2:14:1
sources.quote: כדרך שאין היונה ממירה בן זוגה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is as a dove does not exchange her mate.

sources.quote: קראה יונתי לפי שהיונה יש לה סגולה משאר הבעלי חיים שלא תזדווג כי אם אל הזכר אשר נולד עמה
sources.says: Ralbag says he called her יונתי because the dove, unlike other animals, pairs only with the male that was born with her.

2:14.headline: בחגוי: cracks in the rock, or high places?
2:14.body: Rashi says it means clefts, from a word for breaking, and cites יחוגו וינועו. Metzudat Zion also says cracks and splits. Ibn Ezra says it comes from חוג הארץ, the circle of the earth, so a high place.

sources.quote: בִּנְקִיקֵי, וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן שֶׁבֶר, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ "יָחוֹגּוּ וְיָנוּעוּ"
sources.says: Rashi says it means clefts, and is the language of breaking, like יחוגו וינועו.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 2:14:1
sources.quote: ענין בקוע וחריץ כמו שוכני בחגוי סלע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a split or a crack, as in שוכני בחגוי סלע.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 2:14:1
sources.quote: מן חוג הארץ [והוא הפוך או הם ב׳ שרשים וטעם] מקום גבוה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is from חוג הארץ, a high place.

2:17.headline: הרי בתר: a place name, or "mountains of division"?
2:17.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say בתר means division and distance, as in ויבתר אותם, so the mountains are set apart from each other. Metzudat David adds that it may be a place, named after וילכו כל הבתרון.

sources.quote: בָתֶר. לְשׁוֹן חֲלֻקָּה וְהַפְלָגָה
sources.says: Rashi says בתר is the language of division and separation.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 2:17:8
sources.quote: בתר. ענין חלוקה והפלגה כמו ויבתר אותם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says בתר means division and separation, as in ויבתר אותם.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 2:17:1
sources.quote: ויתכן שהמחוז שעמדו שם הוא על שם וילכו כל הבתרון
sources.says: Metzudat David says it may be that the region they stood in is named for וילכו כל הבתרון.

3:3.headline: Who are the watchmen?
3:3.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra, reading the song as Israel's story, say the watchmen are Moses and Aaron. Ralbag, reading it as the soul's search, says they are the senses, which guard the body.

sources.quote: מְצָאוּנִי הַשֹּׁמְרִים. משֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the watchmen are Moses and Aaron.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 3:3:1
sources.quote: השומרים. הם משה ואהרן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra, in his third reading, also says they are Moses and Aaron.

sources.quote: ראוי שתדע שהחושים הם השומרים
sources.says: Ralbag says the senses are the watchmen, since they were placed in the body to guard it.

3:4.headline: "The room of the one who conceived me"
3:4.body: הורתי comes from הריון, pregnancy. Metzudat Zion says it repeats "my mother" in other words. Malbim says it adds something: a mother may be the one who raised you, while this is the room where you were carried.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 3:4:3
sources.quote: הורתי. מלשון הריון ורוצה לומר אמי שהרתה אותי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from pregnancy and means the mother who conceived me.

sources.quote: שמוסיף על בית אמו שגדלה אותו, החדר שבו ישבה הורתו בעת ההריון
sources.says: Malbim says the verse adds to 'my mother's house', where she raised him, the room where she stayed while pregnant.

3:6.headline: Smoke rising straight up like a palm tree
3:6.body: תימרות comes from תמר, the date palm. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say the smoke rose tall and straight like a palm. Ibn Ezra thinks columns of smoke got the name from the palm's height.

sources.quote: כְּתִימְרוֹת עָשָׁן. גָּבֹהַּ וְזָקוּף כְּתָמָר
sources.says: Rashi says it means tall and upright like a palm.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 3:6:1
sources.quote: כתמרות. מלשון אילן תמר, ורוצה לומר עמוד עשן זקוף כאילן תמר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from the palm tree and means a column of smoke standing straight like one.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 3:6:1
sources.quote: ואולי נקרא(ו) כן בעבור [שהם דומות ל]גבהות אילני התמרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra suggests they were named for the height of palm trees.

3:6.headline: The spice peddler explains the Torah's word for gossip
3:6.body: A רוכל is a peddler who sells spices. Ibn Ezra uses him to explain the Torah's רכיל, gossip. The peddler buys from one man and sells to another, and the gossip tells one person what he heard from another.

sources.quote: כי הרוכל מעתיק יקנה מזה וימכור לזה והרכיל יגלה לזה מה ששמע מזה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the peddler buys from one and sells to another, and the gossip reveals to one what he heard from another.

sources.quote: רוֹכֵל. בַּשָׂם הַמּוֹכֵר כָּל מִינֵי בְשָׂמִים
sources.says: Rashi says a רוכל is a perfumer who sells all kinds of spices.

3:8.headline: "Held by the sword" means holding the sword
3:8.body: The form אחוזי looks passive, "held". Ibn Ezra compares it to לבוש הבדים, "clothed in linen", and says he knows of no third case like it in the Bible.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 3:8:1
sources.quote: אחוזי חרב. כמו לבוש הבדים ולא אדע שלישי במקרא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra compares it to 'clothed in linen' and says he knows no third example in the Bible.

3:8.headline: Rashi's sword is the tradition that guards the text
3:8.body: Rashi reads the guards as scholars. Their swords are the masorah and memory signs, which keep the exact wording of the Torah from being forgotten.

sources.quote: כְּלֵי זֵינוֹ הֵן מְסֹרֶת וְסִימָנִים, שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִים עַל יָדָם אֶת הַגִּרְסָא וְהַמְסוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא תִשְׁתַּכַּח
sources.says: Rashi says their weapons are the masorah and memory signs, which keep the text and its tradition from being forgotten.

3:9.headline: A one-time word for a wedding canopy or bridal litter
3:9.body: Ibn Ezra says אפריון means a wedding canopy and has no match in the Bible. Metzudat Zion says it is the litter brides are carried in, and that the sages called a bed פוריה because there people are fruitful (פרה) and multiply.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 3:9:1
sources.quote: אפריון. חופה ואין לו דומה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a wedding canopy and there is no other word like it.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 3:9:1
sources.quote: הוא המטה שנושאין בה הכלות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the couch on which brides are carried.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 3:9:1
sources.quote: וכן קראו רז״ל למטה פוריה, ואמרו על שם שפרין ורבין עליה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion adds that the sages called a bed פוריה, because people are fruitful and multiply on it.

3:10.headline: A curtain that "rides" on its poles
3:10.body: מרכב comes from riding. Rashi and Metzudat David say it is the purple curtain, which hangs on poles from pillar to pillar, as if riding on them.

sources.quote: זֶה הַפָּרֹכֶת, שֶׁהָיָה תָלוּי וְ'רוֹכֵב' עַל כְּלוֹנְסָאוֹת מֵעַמּוּד לְעַמּוּד
sources.says: Rashi says it is the Temple curtain, which hung and 'rode' on poles from pillar to pillar.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 3:10:3
sources.quote: זהו הוילון התלוי ורוכב על הכלונסות
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the curtain that hangs and rides on the poles.

3:10.headline: Paved with love, or glowing with it?
3:10.body: Some tie רצוף to a stone pavement. Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion tie it to the glowing coal of Isaiah 6:6, so the inside burns with love. Rashi reads it as laid out like a floor of love.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 3:10:2
sources.quote: י״א שהוא מן רצפת אבנים והנכון בעיני שהוא פעול מן ובידו רצפה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some derive it from a stone pavement, but he thinks it comes from the glowing coal of Isaiah 6:6.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 3:10:4
sources.quote: רצוף. ענין גחלת אש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a burning coal, since the Bible likens great love to fire.

sources.quote: סָדוּר בְּרִצְפַּת אַהֲבָה
sources.says: Rashi says it was arranged like a floor of love.

3:11.headline: Daughters of Zion: those "marked" for God
3:11.body: Rashi hears ציון as מצוינים, marked out. He says these are the children marked for God by circumcision, tefillin and tzitzit.

sources.quote: בָּנִים שֶׁמְּצֻיָּנִין לוֹ בְמִילָה וּבִתְפִלִּין וּבְצִיצִית
sources.says: Rashi says the daughters of Zion are children marked out for God by circumcision, tefillin and tzitzit.

3:11.headline: How Israel came to be called God's "mother"
3:11.body: Who is the king's mother? Rashi brings a parable: a king loved his daughter so much he called her daughter, then sister, then mother. Rashi points to "my nation" in Isaiah 51:4 and says it is written ולאמי, which can be read "my mother".

sources.quote: לֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ אִמִּי
sources.says: Rashi's parable says the king kept loving his daughter until he called her 'my mother'.

sources.quote: ״וּלְאִמִּי״ כְּתִיב
sources.says: Rashi says the word in Isaiah is written so it can be read 'and to my mother'.

3:11.headline: The king's wedding day is the day the Torah was given
3:11.body: Rashi reads the wedding day as the giving of the Torah at Sinai, when Israel crowned God as king. The day of his heart's joy is the day the Tabernacle was dedicated.

sources.quote: יוֹם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁעִטְּרוּהוּ לָהֶם לְמֶלֶךְ וְקִבְּלוּ עֻלּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says his wedding day is the day the Torah was given, when they crowned Him king and accepted His rule.

sources.quote: זֶה שְׁמִינִי לְמִלּוּאִים, שֶׁנִּתְחַנֵּךְ בּוֹ הַמִּשְׁכָּן בַּמִּדְבָּר
sources.says: Rashi says the day of his heart's joy is the eighth day of the dedication, when the Tabernacle was inaugurated.

5:1.headline: He ate the honey reed along with the honey, out of love
5:1.body: יער usually means a forest. Here it means the reed that holds honey. People suck the honey and throw the reed away. Rashi says the lover ate the reed too, out of great love: God accepted even offerings that were not normally fit.

sources.quote: וְ"יַעְרַת" הִיא לְשׁוֹן קָנֶה
sources.says: Rashi says יערת means a reed.

sources.quote: אָכַלְתִּי הַקָּנֶה עִם הַדְּבַשׁ, אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי עִם הָרָאוּי
sources.says: Rashi says 'I ate the reed with the honey' means accepting what is not fit along with what is fit.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 5:1:3
sources.quote: כן יקראו הקנים שגדל בהם הדבש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the reeds in which honey grows are called by this name.

5:2.headline: 'I sleep but my heart is awake': whose heart?
5:2.body: Rashi reads 'my heart' as God, who stays awake to guard Israel while she sleeps. Maimonides reads the verse as the highest human level: a person busy with daily life whose mind never leaves God, as Moses was.

sources.quote: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהוּא צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי עֵר לְשָׁמְרֵנִי וּלְהֵיטִיב לִי
sources.says: Rashi says 'my heart' is God, the rock of my heart, who is awake to guard me and do me good.

sources.quote: בעודו מדבר עם בני אדם ועוסק בצרכי גופו כשכל שכלו מופנה אל ה' יתעלה
sources.says: Maimonides says the verse describes a person who talks with people and sees to his body's needs while his whole mind is turned to God.

sources.quote: אלא אני אומר שהיא דרגת משה רבינו
sources.says: Maimonides says this is not the level of all prophets, but the level of Moses.

5:2.headline: Dew and night drops: reward and punishment, or two rewards
5:2.body: The lover's head is wet with dew and his locks with 'drops of the night'. Rashi reads the dew as gentle reward and the night rain as punishment held ready. He also gives a second reading: both are rewards, for easy and for hard commandments.

sources.quote: אַף בְּיָדִי הַרְבֵּה קְבוּצוֹת מִינֵי פֻרְעָנִיּוֹת לִפָּרַע מֵעוֹזְבַי וּמִמְּנַאֲצַי
sources.says: Rashi says the drops stand for many kinds of punishment ready for those who leave and scorn God.

sources.quote: וְיֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ "טַל וּרְסִיסֵי לָיְלָה" שְׁנֵיהֶם לְטוֹבָה
sources.says: Rashi says one may also read both the dew and the night drops as good things, reward for light and heavy commandments.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 5:2:5
sources.quote: ענין זלוף ונטיפה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says רסיס means sprinkling and dripping.

5:6.headline: Her beloved 'slipped away': hid himself, or turned and went
5:6.body: חמק is a rare verb. Rashi says he hid and covered himself, as the thigh is a hidden part of the body. Metzudat Zion says he turned around. Ibn Ezra says he waited a little and then left.

sources.quote: נִסְתַּר וְנִכְסָה מִמֶּנִּי, כְּמוֹ "חַמּוּקֵי יְרֵכַיִךְ"
sources.says: Rashi says he hid and covered himself from me, as in 'the curves of your thighs', which are hidden.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 5:6:1
sources.quote: ענין סבוב כמו עד מתי תתחמקין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means turning around, as in Jeremiah's 'how long will you turn this way and that'.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 5:6:1
sources.quote: המתין מעט ועבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he waited a little and passed on.

5:11.headline: His head is 'ketem': a king's treasure, or a solid lump
5:11.body: כתם is a rare word for gold. Rashi says it means the treasure kings store away. Malbim reads it as a solid lump of metal, whose inside is closed and hidden.

sources.quote: כֶּתֶם הוּא לְשׁוֹן סְגֻלַּת מְלָכִים שֶׁאוֹצְרִין בְּבֵית גִּנְזֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says כתם means the treasure that kings keep in their storehouses.

sources.quote: הכתם הוא עשת מקשה, שזה מורה שפנימיותו סתום וחתום
sources.says: Malbim says כתם is a solid lump, which shows that its inside is sealed and closed.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 5:11:1
sources.quote: זהב טוב ויקר כמו בכתם אופז
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is good and precious gold.

5:11.headline: Black as a raven: the Torah written in black fire
5:11.body: His locks are black as a raven. Rashi reads this as the Torah, written before God in black fire on white fire. Malbim says black swallows light, a picture of what stays hidden.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהָיְתָה כְתוּבָה לְפָנָיו אֵשׁ שְׁחוֹרָה עַל גַּבֵּי אֵשׁ לְבָנָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is because the Torah was written before Him in black fire on white fire.

sources.quote: צבע השחור הוא הבולע את האור בתוכו
sources.says: Malbim says black is the color that swallows light into itself.

5:14.headline: 'Covered' with sapphires, or adorned with them
5:14.body: Both commentators point to Tamar, who ותתעלף before meeting Judah. Metzudat Zion reads that word as wrapping and covering. Rashi follows the Aramaic Targum, which reads it as 'adorned', so the body is decorated with sapphires.

sources.quote: מְקוּשֶּׁטֶת וּמְתוּקֶּנֶת בְּסַפִּירִים, לְשׁוֹן "וַתִּתְעַלָּף", דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינָן וְאִתַּקְנַת
sources.says: Rashi says it means adorned with sapphires, like ותתעלף, which the Targum renders 'she adorned herself'.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 5:14:6
sources.quote: ענין עטוף וכסוי כמו ותתעלף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means wrapped and covered, as in ותתעלף.

5:15.headline: Pillars of 'shesh': marble, or the six sides of the world
5:15.body: שש here means marble, as in the book of Esther. Malbim also hears the number six in it: the legs are the six directions of the world.

sources.quote: עַמּוּדֵי שַׁיִשׁ, וַחֲבֵרוֹ בִמְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says it means marble pillars, as in the book of Esther.

sources.quote: שהם עמודי שש ר"ל שש קצות העולם
sources.says: Malbim says the pillars of שש are the six ends of the world.

5:15.headline: בחור here means 'chosen', like the cedar among trees
5:15.body: בחור usually means a young man. Rashi and Metzudat David read it as 'chosen': the beloved stands out as the cedar stands out among all trees.

sources.quote: נִבְחָר בֵּין הַבָּנִים כְּאֶרֶז בֵּין שְׁאָר עֵצִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means chosen among the young men, like a cedar among other trees.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 5:15:2
sources.quote: והוא נבחר משאר הדודים כארזים מכל עצי היער
sources.says: Metzudat David says he is chosen over other lovers, as cedars are over all the trees of the forest.

6:4.headline: A city's name that also sounds like 'pleasing'
6:4.body: Tirzah was a royal city of the kings of Israel. Rashi, following the Sifrei, also hears רצויה, 'pleasing', in it: you are beautiful when you are pleasing to me.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 6:4:1
sources.quote: שם עיר מלוכה למלכי ישראל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Tirzah is the name of a royal city of the kings of Israel.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁאַתְּ רְצוּיָה לִי. כָּךְ הוּא נִדְרַשׁ בְּסִפְרֵי
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'when you are pleasing to me', and says this is how the Sifrei explains it.

sources.quote: ע"י שנתרצית אלי שנית ושב רצוני עליך
sources.says: Malbim reads it as 'because you made peace with me again and my favor returned to you'.

6:5.headline: Her eyes overwhelm him, or make him bold
6:5.body: The root רהב is about force and pride. Rashi says her eyes made his heart swell, while Ibn Ezra says they either overpowered him or took away his pride.

sources.quote: הֵגֵסוּ לִבִּי, כְּמוֹ וְרָהְבָּם עָמָל וָאָוֶן
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'they made my heart swell', like the pride in Psalm 90:10.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 6:5:1
sources.quote: חזקו ממני או הסירו רהבי וממשלתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra gives two readings: they were stronger than me, or they removed my pride and my rule.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 6:5:2
sources.quote: ענין התחזקות כמו תרהיבני בנפשי עוז
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means growing strong, as in Psalm 138:3.

6:6.headline: A word for losing a child, used for a missing tooth
6:6.body: This word is about a mother who has lost her young. Metzudat Zion says it is borrowed here to mean a gap or a flaw: none of her teeth is missing or damaged.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 6:6:2
sources.quote: רוצה לומר חסרון ופגם ואמר בלשון השאלה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a lack or a flaw, and that the word is used here in a borrowed sense.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 6:6:2
sources.quote: רוצה לומר לא נחסר אחד מהם ולא נפגם
sources.says: Metzudat David says not one tooth is missing and none is damaged.

6:7.headline: A veil that hides the face
6:7.body: Metzudat Zion says צמה here is the veil that covers the face, as in Isaiah 47:2. Metzudat David adds that a face seen through a veil draws more love than one left uncovered.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 6:7:4
sources.quote: היא המסוה המכסה את הפנים וכן גלי צמתך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the veil that covers the face, as in Isaiah 47:2.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 6:7:1
sources.quote: ובזה ממשיכים אהבה וחשק יותר מאילו היו גלוים מבלי מסוה
sources.says: Metzudat David says being hidden draws more love and desire than if they were uncovered.

6:8.headline: Sixty queens, read as a hidden count of nations
6:8.body: The commentators treat the number as a real count. Rashi adds up Abraham's descendants listed in Chronicles and reaches sixty, while Metzudat David counts sixty nations that came from Noah's son Shem.

sources.quote: אַבְרָהָם וְיוֹצְאֵי יְרֵכוֹ. בְּנֵי קְטוּרָה שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה
sources.says: Rashi says the sixty are Abraham and his descendants, starting with the sixteen sons of Keturah.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 6:8:1
sources.quote: זרעו של שם בן נח נחלק אחר כך לששים עממים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the descendants of Shem, son of Noah, later split into sixty nations.

6:9.headline: Pure, or picked out as the best
6:9.body: Metzudat Zion reads ברה as clear and clean. Malbim reads it as chosen: as if her mother picked out all the beauty in the world to make her.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 6:9:1
sources.quote: ברה. מלשון ברור ונקי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means clear and clean.

sources.quote: והיא ברה ונבחרת ליולדתה. כאילו יולדתה בררה לעצמה היופי והחן הנמצא בתבל
sources.says: Malbim says she is chosen, as if her mother selected the beauty and grace found in the world.

6:10.headline: A verb for looking down from a height
6:10.body: Rashi says this verb means looking down from a high place to a low one. For him she is like the Temple, which stands higher than all lands.

sources.quote: מִמָּקוֹם הַגָּבֹהַּ לַנָּמוּךְ קְרוּיָה הַשְׁקָפָה. כָּךְ בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ גָּבֹהַּ מִכָּל אֲרָצוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says looking from a high place to a low one is called השקפה, and so the Temple is higher than all lands.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 6:10:1
sources.quote: ענין ראיה והבטה כמו בעד החלון נשקפה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means seeing and gazing, as in Judges 5:28, looking out through the window.

6:10.headline: Dawn, or the morning star?
6:10.body: Rashi reads שחר as the dawn, which grows brighter little by little, like Israel in the Second Temple period. Metzudat Zion reads it as the morning star, so she grows brighter in steps: star, then moon, then sun.

sources.quote: הוֹלֵךְ וּמֵאִיר מְעַט מְעַט, כָּךְ הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי
sources.says: Rashi says dawn grows brighter little by little, and so was Israel in the Second Temple period.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 6:10:2
sources.quote: שחר. כוכב השחר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שחר here is the morning star.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 6:10:1
sources.quote: כזוהר כוכב השחר, ולאחר זה נתעלתה עד שנעשית יפה כלבנה
sources.says: Metzudat David says she first shone like the morning star and then rose until she was as beautiful as the moon.

6:11.headline: Why Israel is compared to a nut
6:11.body: Rashi says a nut looks like plain wood until you crack it and find food inside, and Israel's scholars are humble in the same way. Ibn Ezra says the nut's fruit is hidden, as God's miracles are hidden in exile.

sources.quote: לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לֶאֱגוֹז? מָה אֱגוֹז זֶה, אַתָּה רוֹאֶה אוֹתוֹ כֻלּוֹ עֵץ וְאֵין נִכָּר מַה בְּתוֹכוֹ
sources.says: Rashi asks why Israel is compared to a nut, and answers that a nut looks like wood outside and you cannot tell what is inside.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 6:11:5
sources.quote: וענין אגוז [שהוא פריו גנוז] והענין שלא יראה נסיו בגלות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the nut's fruit is hidden, meaning God will not show his miracles in exile.

6:12.headline: 'My people', or simply 'a noble people'?
6:12.body: Read plainly, עמי means 'my people', but Rashi says the final yod is extra, as in שכני סנה, so it means 'a noble people'. Ralbag adds that read as one word it is a person's name.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ עַם נָדִיב. יו"ד יְתֵרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'a noble people', and the yod is extra.

sources.quote: קרא זה הכללות עמינדיב אשר הוא שם אדם להעלים הענין
sources.says: Ralbag says the verse uses עמינדיב, a person's name, to hide its meaning, and that it can also be read as 'a noble people' with an extra yod.

7:1.headline: The Shulamite: the whole one, or the woman from Shalem
7:1.body: השולמית sounds like שלם, whole or complete. Rashi reads it as the one whose faith is whole. Ibn Ezra reads it as a woman from Shalem, which is Jerusalem.

sources.quote: הַשְּׁלֵמָה בֶאֱמוּנָתֵךְ עִמּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the one who is whole in her faith with him.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 7:1:1
sources.quote: שהיא ממדינת שלם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says she is from the city of Shalem, which is Jerusalem.

sources.quote: קראה שולמית להיותו נגזר משלמות
sources.says: Ralbag says she is called Shulamite because the name comes from the word for completeness.

7:2.headline: Round jewels, or the hollow pits under the altar
7:2.body: חלאים is a rare word. Rashi says it means a set of gold ornaments, and gives the Arabic word for it. He adds that the sages read it as the round pits under the altar where wine was poured.

sources.quote: אלחל"י בְּלָשׁוֹן עַרְבִי. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָרְשׁוּ עַל נִקְבֵי הַשִּׁיתִין
sources.says: Rashi says the word is the Arabic name for gold ornaments, and that the sages read it as the pits under the altar.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 7:2:2
sources.quote: עדי עגול מקובץ כמו וחלי כתם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a round ornament, like the gold jewel in Proverbs.

7:3.headline: Her navel, or a jeweled belt
7:3.body: Most readers take שררך as the navel. Ibn Ezra also offers a second reading: a belt with a round gem set in it, like the moon.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 7:3:1
sources.quote: הוא הטבור כמו ואונו בשרירי בטנו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the navel, and points to a verse in Job about the muscles of the belly.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 7:3:6
sources.quote: שררך. חגור ובאבנט אבן יקרה עגולה כירח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra's second reading is a belt with a round precious stone like the moon.

7:3.headline: Fenced with lilies: a fence soft enough to break, yet nobody does
7:3.body: סוגה comes from סייג, a fence. Rashi notes that a hedge of lilies could be pushed aside by anyone. Yet Israel stops at it, because a small rule is enough to hold them back.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 7:3:6
sources.quote: מלשון סייג וגדר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from סייג, a fence.

sources.quote: דַּי לָהּ בְּגָדֵר קַל, וְאֵין אֶחָד מֵהֶם פּוֹרֵץ בּוֹ לִכָּנֵס
sources.says: Rashi says a light fence is enough for her, and none of them breaks through it.

7:5.headline: Her eyes like pools of water, or like doves
7:5.body: ברכות usually means pools. Rashi offers a second reading from the language of the Mishnah, where בריכה means a brood of doves. Then her eyes are compared to doves.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 7:5:2
sources.quote: מקום בנוי באבנים ובסיד ושם מתכנסים המים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a ברכה is a place built of stone and plaster where water gathers.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ "יוֹנִים" וּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says it can also be read as doves, a sense found in the language of the Mishnah.

7:5.headline: The town of Heshbon, and the sages' calculations
7:5.body: חשבון is the name of a town, and it also means calculation. Rashi uses both: the eyes of the people are its sages, busy with calculating the seasons and the stars.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 7:5:2
sources.quote: כמו הברכות שבעיר חשבון
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it plainly as the pools in the town of Heshbon.

sources.quote: וַעֲסוּקִים בְּחֶשְׁבּוֹן תְּקוּפוֹת וּמַזָּלוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the sages are busy calculating the seasons and the constellations.

7:5.headline: A nose like a tower? Rashi reads it as her face
7:5.body: אף usually means nose. Rashi says a big nose like a tower is no praise, so here אפך must mean the face, and in particular the forehead. Others keep the plain sense: a straight nose.

sources.quote: אֵינִי יָכוֹל לְפָרְשׁוֹ לְשׁוֹן חֹטֶם
sources.says: Rashi says he cannot read it as nose, and reads it as the face instead.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 7:5:3
sources.quote: דמה החוטם [למגדל] שהוא שוה בלי עוות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reads it as the nose, compared to a tower because it is straight.

7:6.headline: Like Mount Carmel, or like a deep red dye
7:6.body: כרמל is a mountain. Ibn Ezra reads it here as a color, a red dye, the same as כרמיל in Chronicles. That fits the purple in the next half of the verse.

sources.quote: וְכַרְמֶל הוּא רֹאשׁ הֶהָרִים
sources.says: Rashi reads it as Mount Carmel, the chief of the mountains.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 7:6:1
sources.quote: עין [צבע ואומ׳ שהוא עין שני]
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a color, a red dye, like כרמיל in Chronicles.

7:10.headline: Wine that makes sleeping lips murmur
7:10.body: דובב means to make lips move and murmur, from a root of speech. Rashi reads the sleepers as the ancestors in their graves, who rejoice and give thanks.

sources.quote: אַף אֲבוֹתַי בַּקֶּבֶר יִשְׂמְחוּ בִי
sources.says: Rashi says even the ancestors in the grave will rejoice, and that the word means to murmur, from the root for speech.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 7:10:1
sources.quote: מרחש מלשון דבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means murmuring, from the word דבה, a report.

7:12.headline: Spend the night in the villages, or among the deniers
7:12.body: כפרים means villages. Rashi reads the same letters as כופרים, those who deny God. Israel invites God to come and see the people He blessed who now deny Him.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 7:12:3
sources.quote: כן יקראו המקומות הקטנות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says כפרים are small places, villages.

sources.quote: נָלִינָה בַּכּוֹפְרִים. בֹּא וְאַרְאֶךָ בְּנֵי עֵשָׂו
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'let us lodge among the deniers', and says Israel will show God the children of Esau who deny Him.

7:14.headline: Mandrakes, or baskets of good and bad figs
7:14.body: דודאים is the plant from the story of Rachel and Leah. Rashi reads it as baskets, like the two baskets of figs in Jeremiah. Both the good and the bad figs now give off a scent, so all of Israel seeks God.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 7:14:1
sources.quote: שם עשב כדמות אדם זכר ונקבה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a plant shaped like a man and a woman, as in Genesis 30.

sources.quote: דּוּדָאֵי הַתְּאֵנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת וְהָרָעוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says these are the baskets of good and bad figs from Jeremiah.

8:2.headline: Same word: kiss in one verse, give drink in the next
8:2.body: In verse 1 אשקך means "I would kiss you". In verse 2 the same letters mean "I would give you to drink", from a different root.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 8:1:3
sources.quote: אשקך.} מלשון נשיקה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion reads אשקך in verse 1 as coming from the word for kissing.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 8:2:2
sources.quote: אשקך.} ענין שתיה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion reads אשקך in verse 2 as meaning drinking.

8:2.headline: Who teaches her: the beloved, or her mother?
8:2.body: The form תלמדני can mean "you will teach me" or "she will teach me". Ibn Ezra says it is her mother who teaches. Metzudat David reads it as the beloved teaching her.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 8:2:1
sources.quote: תלמדני. התי״ו חוזר לאמי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the letter tav points back to "my mother", so the mother is the one who teaches.

sources.ref: Metzudat David on Song of Songs 8:2:1
sources.quote: למען תלמד אותי שמה במה אתרצה לך
sources.says: Metzudat David explains it as the beloved teaching her there how to please him.

8:4.headline: This time the oath says "why" instead of "if"
8:4.body: Earlier in the book this oath reads "if you wake love". Here it reads מה, "why would you wake", meaning it would do no good.

sources.quote: ולא אמרה להם אם תעירו וגו' אבל אמרה מה תעירו
sources.says: Ralbag notes she did not say "if you wake" but "why would you wake", to show the effort could not succeed.

sources.quote: מַה תָּעִירוּ וּמַה תְּעֹרְרוּ.} כִּי לֹא יוֹעִיל לָכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the question means it will not help you.

8:5.headline: A word found only here, explained from Arabic
8:5.body: מתרפקת, "leaning on" or "clinging to", appears nowhere else in the Bible. Rashi, Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion all explain it from an Arabic word for joining or company.

sources.quote: "רפק" בְּלָשׁוֹן עַרְבִי רפקתא, חֲבוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the root רפק in Arabic means companionship, so she is joined to her beloved.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 8:5:1
sources.quote: ענין התחברות ודבוק ואין לו דמיון במקרא והוא מלשון ערבי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means joining and clinging, has no parallel in Scripture, and comes from Arabic.

sources.ref: Ibn Ezra on Song of Songs 8:5:1
sources.quote: מתרפקת. מתחברת וכן בלשון קדר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means joining, and that this is its sense in Arabic.

8:6.headline: God's name, Yah, is tucked into the word for flame
8:6.body: שלהבתיה ends in יה, a name of God. Metzudat Zion says the Bible adds God's name to make a thing great, so this is a huge flame.

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 8:6:6
sources.quote: כי כן דרך המקרא כשרוצה להגדיל דבר מה סומכו למלת השם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Scripture attaches God's name to a thing when it wants to show it is great.

sources.quote: לוֹמַר "אֵשׁ שֶׁל שַׁלְהֶבֶתְיָה"
sources.says: Rashi uses the accent marks to read the phrase as "fire of the shalhevetyah".

8:8.headline: Rashi hears "sister" as "the one who joins with us"
8:8.body: אחות means sister. Rashi links it to a word for mending or joining together, so the sister is the one who clings to us.

sources.quote: שֶׁהִיא מִתְאַחָה וּמִתְחַבֶּרֶת וּמִתְאַוָּה לִהְיוֹת עִמָּנוּ
sources.says: Rashi says she joins and attaches herself and wants to be with us.

sources.quote: אֲחוֹת.} לְשׁוֹן אִחוּי
sources.says: Rashi says the word comes from the idea of mending, like torn cloth that cannot be mended.

8:9.headline: Malbim hears longing inside the word for silver
8:9.body: כסף means silver, but the same root also means to long for. Malbim reads the "turret of silver" as a place of longing.

sources.quote: בטירה חזקה העשויה מכסף הכוסף
sources.says: Malbim calls it a strong turret made of the silver of longing, meaning a husband she will long for.

sources.quote: אל הטירה הנכספת לצדיקים
sources.says: In his reading of the allegory, Malbim calls it the turret the righteous long for.

8:13.headline: The "the" here is a call: "O you who sit"
8:13.body: The letter ה at the start of היושבת is not "the". Metzudat Zion says it calls out to someone, so the verse means "you who sit in the gardens".

sources.ref: Metzudat Zion on Song of Songs 8:13:1
sources.quote: בה״א הקריאה כמו הדור אתם ראו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the ה is the ה of calling out, as in "O generation, see".
